History and Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old male with 6-week history of generalized fatigue and diffuse musculoskeletal aches following travel to the United States; transient erythematous calf rash in late February; plan for blood work including Lyme serology and routine panels.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Feeling “aching all over,” tired and run-down for ≈6 weeks.  
• Onset / course: Last felt well around Christmas/New Year. Returned from U.S. holiday end-Jan/early-Feb; symptoms began ≈2 weeks after return. Persistently present since, no clear progression described.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Decreased energy and daytime tiredness; reduced exercise tolerance.  
  – ↓ appetite (smaller portions) but no reported weight change.  
  – Occasional mild headache; no focal neurologic symptoms.  
  – Diffuse joint/soft-tissue aches (shoulders, back, hips, knees) without swelling.  
• Denied symptoms: No fever at present, no respiratory (cough, SOB), ENT, GI (nausea, vomiting, abd pain, diarrhea, blood in stool), GU (dysuria, hematuria), skin rash currently, or peripheral swelling.  
• Notable event: Single oval rash on posterior calf (photo shown); appeared mid-/late-Feb, faded over ≈2 weeks; minimally pruritic; occurred after walking/hiking in shorts; no recalled insect/tick bite.  
• Stress / mood: Feels psychologically well; prior stress issues resolved.  
• Impact: Continues to work (health technology company) but feels less effective; exercise reduced.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – stable; uses preventative inhaler twice daily. No recent exacerbations.  
• Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.  
( No other chronic conditions mentioned.)

Medications:
• Preventative asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (patient reports morning & night use).  
• Oral antihistamine – dose/route/frequency not documented (OTC).  

Allergies:
• Not documented.

Social History:
• Lives with wife.  
• Occupation: Health technology company (office-based).  
• Smoking: Not clearly stated (information missing).  
• Alcohol: Occasional use.  
• Recent travel: United States, end-Jan to early-Feb; extensive walking/hiking in shorts and boots → possible tick exposure.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed / not documented during virtual visit.

Investigations:
• Planned:  
  – Full blood count.  
  – Renal and liver function tests.  
  – Additional “normal things” per physician (exact panels not specified).  
  – Lyme disease serology.  
  – Other infection/“reduced energy” screens (e.g., thyroid, inflammatory markers) implied but not specified.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Persistent fatigue with myalgias/arthralgias, decreased appetite – 6 weeks.  
  • Differential includes post-infectious fatigue, endocrine/metabolic causes, anemia, inflammatory or rheumatologic disease.  
  • Plan: Order comprehensive blood work (FBC, U&E, LFTs, thyroid, CRP/ESR).

Issue 2: Possible Lyme disease (erythema migrans-like rash + systemic symptoms after U.S. hiking).  
  • Plan: Lyme serology.  
  • If positive → initiate appropriate antibiotic regimen (e.g., doxycycline) per guidelines.

Issue 3: General health monitoring.  
  • Plan: Review inhaler adherence; continue preventative inhaler.  
  • Continue antihistamine for hay fever as needed.

General plan items:  
• Patient to arrange blood tests through support line.  
• Schedule telephone follow-up ≈1 week after labs to discuss results and next steps.  
• Advise to seek care sooner if symptoms worsen (fever, neurologic changes, joint swelling).
